answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making influence slow-earned rather than instantly claimed: a new identity starts with zero voting weight and must build a ferrous, hard-to-forge record of signed, peer-verified jobs over many epochs. Like pigment that marks one genuine batch, the registry ties each job to a single auditable history, so identical work cannot be replayed across clones. A whole tundra of fresh copies therefore stays weightless until each one separately earns trust, while a proven agent keeps its standing.
